result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_isomorphic()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if this graph is isomorphic to another graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4395-L4496){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_isomorphic(other) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Two graphs are isomorphic if there exists a one-to-one correspondence (bijection) between their nodes that preserves the adjacency relationship. In simpler terms, they have the same structure but possibly different node labels. This implementation checks the following necessary conditions: - same number of nodes - same number of edges - same degree sequence - same directedness ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Another `Graph` object to compare with. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if graphs satisfy isomorphism conditions, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} This is a heuristic check using necessary but not sufficient conditions. It will correctly identify *non-isomorphic* graphs (returning `False`) but may give false positives. A complete isomorphism test requires algorithms like VF2. This method is useful as a fast filter before more expensive isomorphism tests. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two paths of the same length are isomorphic even though their node labels differ -- what matters is the structure, not the names: ::: {#51b45f14 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g1 = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) g2 = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="X") .add_node(label="Y") .add_node(label="Z") .add_edge("X", "Y") .add_edge("Y", "Z") ) g1.is_isomorphic(g2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: A path and a star of the same size have different degree sequences, so they're correctly ruled out: ::: {#604590c1 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} path = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_path_graph(n=4) star = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_star_graph(n=4) path.is_isomorphic(star) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Directedness is compared too, so an otherwise-identical directed and undirected graph don't count as isomorphic: ::: {#7dc007d5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} directed = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_path_graph(n=3) undirected = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_path_graph(n=3) directed.is_isomorphic(undirected) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Two complete graphs of the same size are always isomorphic, since every node is interchangeable: ::: {#6f94b4c2 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} k4_a = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_full_graph(n=4) k4_b = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_full_graph(n=4) k4_a.is_isomorphic(k4_b) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Graphs of different sizes can never be isomorphic: ::: {#5770f4bb .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} g3 = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_cycle_graph(n=3) g4 = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_cycle_graph(n=4) g3.is_isomorphic(g4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` False ``` ::: :::
